items.title: Bumble ditches its rule that kept men from making the first move
items.summary: Bumble is ditching the rule that it has enforced since launching in 2024. Men can finally message first.

items.title: North Korean remote IT staffer worked for US government agency, says FBI
items.summary: The investigation shows that North Koreans are able to infiltrate government agencies, as well as private organizations and crypto exchanges.

items.title: Spotify will label ‘AI Persona’ profiles and exclude their music from recommendations
items.summary: Spotify is introducing “AI Persona” labels for artist profiles that represent AI-generated identities and will exclude their music from editorial, algorithmic, and personalized recommendations by defa...

items.title: What comes after the smartphone? Amazon’s Panos Panay will make his case at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
items.summary: At Disrupt 2026, Amazon's Panos Panay will provide an exclusive vision for what's in store for us beyond the smartphone.

items.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
items.summary: Anthropic will extend support for watermarking AI generations for older models as well.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly completed a $7 billion employee tender offer
items.summary: San Francisco's housing market is in trouble again.

items.title: As AI-led attacks multiply, OpenAI launches a new cyber model
items.summary: OpenAI is expanding its AI cybersecurity defense program Daybreak, and rolling out a new cyber-trained AI model with it.

items.title: Jeff Bezos might finally get his hands on a sports team
items.summary: Jeff Bezos is reportedly close to buying his first stake in a sports team: the U.K.'s famed Liverpool Football Club.

items.title: Now Rippling is counter-suing tiny startup Runlayer
items.summary: This lawsuit follows one filed last month by Runlayer that accused Rippling of stealing its product ideas. It's a seller- and buyer-beware market warning.

items.title: Google co-founder Sergey Brin has now spent $100 million to fight the billionaire tax
items.summary: California's Prop 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state's billionaires.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg’s AI manifesto is exactly why people don’t like AI
items.summary: On Monday, Mark Zuckerberg published a 6,500-word manifesto about personal AI, largely about the possibilities for the "personal superintelligence" systems Meta AI is building.

items.title: Tech industry is buzzing after a Claude agent hacked into a gym
items.summary: An OpenClaw agent hacked into a gym's reservation system to bump its human boss higher on a class' waitlist. And the tech industry took notice.

items.title: Aptoide becomes the first rival app store to return to Google Play in the US
items.summary: Aptoide has brought its games store back to Google Play after more than a decade, as court-ordered changes open Android to competing app stores.

items.title: Social media platforms still facing thousands of user addiction lawsuits after failed appeals
items.summary: Platforms like Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, and Google are facing a long road of litigation.

items.title: YouTube now requires creators to have twice as many watch hours to start earning money
items.summary: Creators who want to start earning on the platform will need at least 8,000 qualified watch hours over the past year or 20 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days.

items.title: Clicks’ Power Keyboard brings BlackBerry-style typing to any phone — with some compromises
items.summary: Clicks’ $99 Power Keyboard brings a customizable, slide-out physical keyboard to MagSafe and Qi2 smartphones, but its added heft can make larger phones awkward to use.

items.title: Meta’s new Glimmer AI model offers a hint at Zuckerberg’s personal intelligence vision
items.summary: Meta’s new open-weight Muse Glimmer model offers a glimpse of Mark Zuckerberg’s personal superintelligence vision, as well as  the emerging divide between AI users can own and access.

items.title: Sila lands $1.4B Pentagon loan as militaries demand more batteries
items.summary: Battery materials startup Sila will use a $1.4 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Defense to scale production at its factory in Washington state.

items.title: Archer buys former rival Wisk Aero
items.summary: The two companies were once embroiled in a trade secret theft lawsuit. Now, Wisk is being absorbed into Archer.

items.title: A data breach at shipping giant Ceva Logistics is rippling across banks, retailers, Steam gamers, and beyond
items.summary: Companies that rely on Ceva Logistics for shipping their physical goods to customers say their personal data was taken during a recent cyberattack.
